article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Hybrid
Genetics: Blueberry Sativa × Blueberry male
Breeder: DJ Short
THC Content: 20–24%
CBD Content: Generally low
Terpene Profile: caryophyllene , linalool , myrcene
Primary Flavors: Vanilla, honey, sweet melon, flowers
Flowering Time (Indoor): 55–60 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: late September through October
Indoor Yield: Moderate to medium-high
Outdoor Yield: Moderate to medium-high
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Some cannabis strains announce themselves through aggressive fuel, sharp skunk, or syrupy fruit. Vanilluna takes the opposite approach. Its attraction lies in detail rather than volume: creamy vanilla, warm honey, flowers, and sweet melon unfold gradually from resin-coated buds with an old-school Kush-like appearance. DJ Short developed the cultivar entirely within his celebrated Blueberry family , but the finished marijuana does not simply repeat the familiar blueberry flavor associated with that line. Instead, it explores a softer and more unusual corner of those genetics, pairing a dreamy, remarkably long-lasting high with an aromatic profile that can resemble vanilla cream, honeyed fruit, and floral musk. Even among DJ Short’s distinctive creations, this is a weed strain with a personality that is difficult to mistake for anything else.
Genetics and Lineage

DJ Short created Vanilluna by crossing a female Blueberry Sativa with the Original Blueberry male he described as a “stretch indica.” The female came from the exact seed stock that also produced the mother used for Blue Satellite. According to the breeder, that selected plant was large, green, symmetrical, strongly centered around a dominant main stem, and equipped with compact nodes and long lateral branches. The Original Blueberry male contributed the broader indica influence while retaining enough vertical vigor to keep the offspring from developing into extremely short plants. DJ Short’s current strain archive continues to identify this same pedigree.

That makes Vanilluna a particularly interesting form of line breeding. Both parents come from DJ Short’s Blueberry genetic pool, yet they represent different expressions within it. Rather than introducing an unrelated strain simply to add a new aroma or increase potency, the breeder combined contrasting Blueberry selections to expose qualities already hidden within the family. The resulting cultivar has sometimes been described as a “quasi-hybrid” because its parents are related genetically while presenting markedly different growth and effect characteristics.

Its family connection also provides useful historical context. DJ Short’s Blueberry work stretches back decades and became foundational to numerous cannabis breeding projects. Vanilluna belongs to a later exploration of that gene pool, emphasizing cream, vanilla, floral notes, and melon rather than concentrating exclusively on the darker berry traits for which Blueberry became famous. The strain is therefore best understood as an internal refinement of classic Blueberry genetics rather than a conventional outcross.
Effects and Experience

Vanilluna develops with an unusual smoothness. Instead of delivering a sudden surge of mental stimulation or dropping immediately into a heavy body stone, the experience tends to unfold slowly into a clear, comfortable headspace. Mood may brighten, thoughts become less hurried, and ordinary surroundings can take on a softer, more absorbing quality. DJ Short describes the finished effect as exceptionally long-lasting and dreamy, language that fits the strain better than simple labels such as “energizing” or “sedating.”

Physical relaxation gradually fills in underneath the cerebral component. The body can feel loose without becoming completely immobilized, while mental clarity is often retained longer than expected. Certain plants selected during DJ Short’s testing produced an experience reminiscent of Blue Heaven, which the breeder characterized as calming, clear, and relatively anti-anxiety. That does not mean every phenotype will behave identically, but it highlights one of the more interesting possibilities within the line.

Greater doses can shift the balance toward deeper relaxation and a more introspective, hazy state. With modern flower sometimes testing above 20% THC, inexperienced cannabis consumers should not assume the gentle aroma indicates mild potency. Dry mouth, dry eyes, dizziness, impaired short-term memory, or excessive sedation remain possible when THC intake exceeds personal tolerance.
Medical Benefits

The unusually calm mental character has made Vanilluna appealing to some medical marijuana consumers who prefer cannabis that does not feel intensely stimulating. A smooth transition from mental ease into physical relaxation may be useful for people seeking temporary relief from everyday stress or tension while remaining relatively functional. Later in the experience, the heavier relaxation can make the strain more appropriate for evenings or quiet periods.

Some consumers also turn to THC-dominant weed for discomfort, appetite loss, nausea, or difficulty sleeping. Those uses should be viewed in the context of cannabis generally rather than as proven medical properties of this particular cultivar. Vanilluna itself has not undergone controlled clinical trials establishing effectiveness for anxiety, insomnia, chronic pain, depression, or other medical disorders.

Individual chemistry matters considerably. THC content, terpene expression, dosage, tolerance, medications, and personal sensitivity can all change the experience. Anyone using marijuana therapeutically should consider laboratory data from the actual batch and consult a qualified healthcare professional when cannabis is being combined with prescription medication or used for a significant health condition.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Vanilluna earns its name through an aroma that is unusually soft and layered. DJ Short describes the profile as a creamy vanilla-and-honey blend accompanied by flowers and sweet melon musk. Those elements can overlap in a way that resembles vanilla custard, honeydew, floral cream, or lightly perfumed fruit rather than the loud berry sweetness someone might expect from its Blueberry ancestry.

Breaking apart the flower can reveal additional depth. Subtle blueberry, earth, herbs, and musk may appear beneath the sweeter notes, while well-developed resin gives the aroma a richer texture late in bloom. The flavor typically begins creamy and lightly sweet, followed by vanilla and honey through the middle. Melon and flowers linger afterward, sometimes accompanied by mild earthy or berry undertones.

Modern commercial descriptions have associated the strain with caryophyllene, linalool, and myrcene, although DJ Short has not published a universal laboratory terpene specification. Because terpene production changes with phenotype, environment, maturity, drying, and storage, these compounds should be treated as common markers rather than guaranteed proportions in every harvest.
Growing Information

Plant structure is one of the best-documented aspects of Vanilluna. DJ Short describes medium-tall, Kush-like plants with short internodal spacing, large dark green foliage, thick hollow stems, and sturdy branching. Flowers form into tight, spade-shaped clusters composed of swollen, somewhat elongated calyxes. As maturity approaches, the surface can become heavily covered in large clear trichomes, creating the frosted appearance typical of quality Blueberry-family cannabis.

Indoor flowering takes approximately 55–60 days. The breeder specifically notes that some of the most interesting aromatic oils develop during the final week, making premature harvest undesirable when flavor is the goal. Yield is generally moderate to medium-high rather than enormous. DJ Short recommends an extended vegetative period combined with early topping to increase production, while untopped plants can also be run in a Sea of Green arrangement.

An unusual genetic feature deserves attention: historical breeder descriptions indicate that roughly 15% of plants may display variegated growth patterns, while the majority remain comparatively uniform apart from differences in final height. This should not automatically be mistaken for disease or nutritional damage. Outdoors, harvest generally falls around late September into October where seasonal conditions permit full maturation. Growers should prioritize completing the final portion of bloom because the strain’s distinctive aromatic character becomes especially pronounced near maturity.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Vanilluna?

Vanilluna is Blueberry Sativa × Original Blueberry “stretch indica.” Both selections come from DJ Short’s Blueberry gene pool. The female was selected from the same seed stock that produced the mother of Blue Satellite, making this a particularly close exploration of contrasting Blueberry expressions.
Is Vanilluna indica or sativa?

It is a balanced indica/sativa hybrid with pronounced Kush-like plant structure. Rather than behaving like a classic heavy indica or energetic sativa, the effects combine mental clarity, dreaminess, and gradual physical relaxation.
What does Vanilluna taste like?

Vanilla and honey form the central flavor, accompanied by sweet melon, creamy floral notes, subtle blueberry, and light earthiness. The aroma is generally softer and more sophisticated than the intense candy profiles found in many newer marijuana hybrids.
How strong is Vanilluna weed?

Modern examples are often reported around 20–24% THC, although DJ Short does not publish a universal breeder-certified potency figure. Actual strength depends on phenotype and cultivation, so laboratory results for a particular batch provide the most reliable measurement.
How long does Vanilluna take to flower?

DJ Short gives an indoor flowering window of approximately 55–60 days, or roughly eight to nine weeks. The breeder emphasizes that important aromatic oils continue developing during the last week, so allowing the plant to reach full maturity can significantly affect the finished flavor.
Final Thoughts on Vanilluna

Vanilluna demonstrates how much variation can exist inside a carefully developed cannabis family. DJ Short did not need to combine Blueberry with an unrelated modern hybrid to create something distinctive. By pairing a Blueberry Sativa female with his Original Blueberry stretch-indica male, he uncovered an expression built around vanilla, honey, flowers, melon, dreamy clarity, and Kush-like structure. The result feels connected to classic Blueberry while occupying its own unmistakable aromatic territory.

For enthusiasts of old-school marijuana genetics, that individuality is the main attraction. Dense spade-shaped flowers, substantial trichome coverage, an eight-to-nine-week flowering cycle, and a smooth long-lived effect give the plant practical as well as historical appeal. More than its dessert-like name suggests, Vanilluna is a thoughtful piece of DJ Short’s broader Blueberry breeding work and one of the more unusual examples of how selective breeding can reveal entirely new sensory qualities from an established cannabis gene pool.
